audit.why: 46.36% over 481 games - by far the largest sample in this slice and the only matchup here where the number carries real weight. It says a near-even lane tilted slightly against Mel, which is what I wrote toward.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer notices that Ritual Nails (Q) and Purgatory (R) both carry the projectile flag, while Mel's Rebuttal is described by Riot as a barrier that 'reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker'. The entry treats Rebuttal purely as a generic 'self-peel for his blink'.
audit.why: This is the largest omission in the matchup. Locke's two highest-value casts are the two things Rebuttal is built to answer, and his execute ultimate is one of them. It reframes the whole W decision: the barrier is not a panic button for the dash, it is an answer aimed at the nails and at Purgatory.
audit.corrected: Ritual Nails and Purgatory are both projectiles, so Rebuttal is a live answer to each.
audit.caveat: Confidence is Medium rather than High deliberately. The kit files establish that these are projectiles and that Rebuttal reflects projectiles, but whether a reflect specifically catches an ultimate is the same class of question as spell-shield eligibility, which the brief marks UNKNOWN and off-limits to assert from file data. The wording I propose says Rebuttal is a live answer, not that the reflected ult executes him. Someone should confirm the ult case on the League Wiki before it is stated harder than that.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer builds its entire counterplay around dodging Q 'recasts' - 'step off the Q recast lines' (breakdown.early), 'sidestep the recasts' (breakdown.cooldowns, report[5]), 'His Q recasts whiffed' (tradeGood, breakdown.trading, dosFull[1].d). Riot's Ritual Nails text describes one throw: 'Locke readies a set of Soul Nails to throw, dealing damage to and marking enemies hit. Locke can consume the marks to deal bonus damage with his attacks.' The marks are cashed through his ATTACKS, not through a recast.
audit.why: It teaches the wrong safety behaviour. A player who believes the danger is a follow-up cast will sidestep and then stand still inside his attack range, which is exactly where the marks get spent. The correct response once marked is to break auto-attack range.
audit.corrected: He cashes marks through his autos - break attack range once marked, rather than watching for a second cast.

audit.whatIsWrong: Silver Stake (P) is never explained. Riot: 'Locke's attacks deal additional magic damage On-Hit, increased based on enemy missing Health.'
audit.why: It compounds viciously with Purgatory. His auto damage rises as Mel's health falls, at exactly the moment his ultimate's execute threshold becomes reachable. The entry tells the reader to 'end fights above his floor' without explaining that the run-up to that floor accelerates against them.
audit.corrected: Silver Stake scales with your missing health, so his autos hit hardest exactly when Purgatory's execute is closest.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] Itemization says 'Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP)' and 'Anti-heal is optional - his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.' Soul Ignition (W) carries the trueDamage flag, so resists miss part of his output. And _missing-interactions.json flags mel vs locke as needs-antiheal on exactly that ability.
audit.why: Both halves point the reader at the wrong purchase. MR is sold as the answer to damage that partly ignores it, and Grievous Wounds is waved off on the reasoning that a self-refund is not healing - but healing reduction applies to healing regardless of its source, and Soul Ignition's refund is the thing that lets him win extended trades against poke.
audit.corrected: Soul Ignition's damage is true, so resists miss that part; bring Grievous Wounds because the refund is what beats chip.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json (W Soul Ignition, kitFlags.trueDamage and heal)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carries one unverifiable claim and no numbers: 'Locke E (Ashen Pursuit): his ONLY mobility, resets on takedowns'. Nothing in Riot's E text mentions a takedown reset - the description is just 'Locke teleports to a location before dashing to attack his next target'. The takedown-scaling clause in this kit belongs to R ('Locke gains additional power for sealing away enemy champions'), not E.
audit.why: A believed E reset changes how you play every skirmish near a dying minion or a kill. If it is not real, the reader disengages from a window that was actually safe. Meanwhile the real numbers were absent: Ritual Nails 10/9/8/7/6, Ashen Pursuit 10 flat at only 425 range, Purgatory 120/100/80.
audit.corrected: Dropped the takedown-reset claim and put the real cooldowns and ranges in.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json (E and R descriptions, cooldowns, ranges)

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree about level 6. full.phases[4].side is 'Locke' with why 'Purgatory changes the rules: fights now end at HIS floor', while content.win[4] is 'Skill' and content.whys[4] says 'Level 6 is still even ... neither ult cleanly wins the exchange yet'.
audit.why: One of them is wrong and they are shown to the same reader. Purgatory is an execute on a 120s cooldown landing on a 550-range mage with no dash; that is the sharper level-6 spike, and the full layer's reading is the defensible one. Unlike the full layer, content.win[] is genuinely editable, so this one is fixable.
audit.corrected: content.win[4] to 'Locke' and whys[4] rewritten to match the full layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[6] Rune Setup is written for somebody else: 'Take your standard rune page for this class - into Locke, prioritize sustain-through-poke (Second Wind/Doran's Shield pattern) if you're melee'. report[7] Summoner Spells opens 'Standard for your champion.'
audit.why: Mel is a 550-range mage. A conditional aimed at melee readers is dead text in a Mel page, and 'standard for your champion' tells a reader nothing they did not already have. Both slots are uniquely addressable here so they can be made concrete.
audit.corrected: Named Mel's actual page and spells.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.spikes[] has 3 entries where every other matchup in this file has 4 - the packet flags this as the only defect on this matchup.
audit.why: The missing beat is the first-item window, which is the one the rest of the entry calls the danger point ('The real danger arrives at his first item', 'His first-item spike is the danger window'). So the spike list omits precisely the spike the prose says decides the lane.
audit.corrected: NOT FIXABLE BY PROPOSAL: the edit format replaces strings at existing paths and cannot append an array element, and the brief forbids changing the number of entries. Needs a manual insert of a 1st-item spike - see notes.

notes: Largest sample in my slice (481 games) and the only fully bespoke full-layer entry - almost every path here is uniquely addressable, so this one took the most edits and needed the fewest workarounds. THREE THINGS THAT NEED A HUMAN. (1) content.spikes[] has 3 entries where the schema expects 4, and the missing one is the first-item spike that the rest of the entry calls the decisive window. The proposal format can only replace strings at existing paths, so this needs a manual insert. (2) SUSPECT DERIVED FLAG, affects more than this matchup: champ-data/_kits/mel.json puts a 'terrain: creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes' flag on Mel's W Rebuttal. Riot's own text is 'Mel forms a barrier around herself that reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker, prevents her from taking damage, and grants her movement speed' - there is no terrain and nothing that blocks a path. That bad flag has already propagated: _missing-interactions.json generates 'Your Rebuttal (W) shuts off Locke's Ashen Pursuit (E)' for this matchup off the back of it. I did NOT write that claim into any text and I would not trust it anywhere else it appears in the file. Worth re-running tools/derive-interactions.js after the flag is fixed. (3) The takedown-reset claim on Ashen Pursuit that I removed from breakdown.cooldowns may appear in other Locke matchups too - nothing in Riot's E text supports it. Unverified and left alone: the 'he's a 125-range mana champ' framing in tldr and phases[0].why. Locke's attack range is not in the kit file and I had no local source for it, so I did not touch it either way.
